title: Health stocks up, tech stocks down on Friday
summary: On the last trading day of the week, healthcare companies on the Nasdaq rose about 2.1% on average, while technology companies slipped about 0.6%.
why: When money moves from one group of stocks to another, people call it a rotation. One day is not a trend, but if it keeps happening, our tech-heavy companies could lag while health companies like Eli Lilly do better.

title: TSMC's sales jumped 55% in a year
summary: TSMC, the factory that builds chips for NVIDIA, AMD and Apple, reported September sales of about NT$512 billion, 54.6% more than a year earlier. Sales for the first nine months of 2026 grew about 41%.
why: TSMC builds the chips that power AI. When its sales keep growing this fast, it means companies are still buying lots of AI chips, which is good news for the AI suppliers on our list.

title: The Fed may raise interest rates again
summary: Notes from the Federal Reserve's last meeting showed most officials expect another rate increase this year, because prices are still rising about 3.4% a year, well above their 2% goal. The Fed already raised rates in September.
why: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive and make safe savings pay more. That can pull money away from stocks, especially fast-growing companies that look expensive, like many AI stocks.

title: Coming up: the Fed decides on rates Oct. 28-29
summary: The Federal Reserve's next meeting is October 28-29. According to the same report, traders expect the Fed to wait at that meeting and raise rates in December.
why: Fed meeting days often make the whole market jumpy. A surprise in either direction can move every stock on our list.

title: Rocket Lab's big new rocket might slip to 2027
summary: Rocket Lab said the window to launch its larger Neutron rocket before the end of 2026 is narrowing, and a filing said the first flight could slip into 2027. A fuel tank broke during a test in January, which already caused a delay.
why: Investors are paying today for rockets Rocket Lab plans to fly tomorrow. Delays push back the money those launches would earn, which is one reason the stock is far below its high.

title: Inflation report due Wednesday
summary: The government will publish September price numbers on Wednesday, Oct. 14. Forecasters expect yearly inflation to rise to about 3.6%, up from 3.4% in August, mostly because gasoline prices were very high. Until the real number comes out, this is only a guess.
why: Inflation is how fast prices go up. If it is higher than people expect, the Fed may keep interest rates high or raise them, and that usually makes stocks that cost a lot compared with their profits, like AMD, fall more.

title: Coming up: the Fed decides on rates Oct. 27-28
summary: Minutes from the Fed's last meeting showed that officials expect another rate increase may be needed this year. The next decision is at the end of October.
why: The Fed sets the rate banks charge each other, and that moves what everyone pays to borrow. Higher rates usually make bonds look better and can pull stock prices down.

title: Microsoft reportedly plans its own AI chip
summary: Press reports say Microsoft plans to show a new chip called Maia 300 and has talked with TSMC about making hundreds of thousands of them for 2027. Microsoft has not confirmed the timing, and reports disagree on when it will arrive.
why: If big companies build their own chips, they may buy fewer from NVIDIA over time. But TSMC would likely make the chips either way, so this is something to watch, not a sure thing.

title: TSMC will report its results on Thursday
summary: TSMC, the world's biggest maker of advanced chips, will share its July to September results on Thursday, Oct. 15, at 2:00 am Eastern time. Its own forecast for the quarter was sales of about $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion.
why: TSMC builds chips for NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom. If it says orders are strong, that is a good clue for those companies too; if it sounds careful, they can fall together. A forecast is not a result, so wait for the real numbers.

title: Meta shares rise after new AI model launch
summary: Meta stock climbed about 2.6% on Tuesday, adding to a jump on Monday. Reports link the rise to the company's new AI models and to analysts raising their price targets. We could not open the article, so the details come from a search summary.
why: Investors pay more for a company when they believe its new products will earn money. But a stock that has already jumped has less room to rise if the news turns out to be smaller than hoped.

title: Inflation report due Wednesday morning
summary: The September consumer price report comes out on Oct. 14 at 8:30 am Eastern. Economists polled by Dow Jones expect prices to rise 0.6% in the month and 3.6% over the past year, helped by higher energy costs. The Fed's next meeting is Oct. 27 and 28.
why: Inflation is how fast prices rise. If it is hotter than expected, investors may think interest rates will stay high or go up, which can pull down stocks that already cost a lot compared with their profits.

title: TSMC reports record sales for July to September
summary: The Taiwanese chipmaker said its sales for the third quarter were about 50% higher than a year before and above what analysts expected. It did not give an outlook yet. That comes with its full earnings report on Thursday, Oct. 15.
why: TSMC builds chips for many AI companies, so strong sales suggest those customers are still buying. The outlook it gives on Thursday matters even more than last quarter's numbers.

title: Eli Lilly slips about 1.3% on Tuesday
summary: Shares of the drugmaker dipped to about $1,167 in lighter than normal trading. The article notes that analysts still lean positive, and also points to questions about how many people stopped taking an experimental weight loss drug in a trial.
why: Drug company shares often move on trial results, since a medicine's success drives future sales. A small dip on low volume is usually not a big signal by itself.
